# Changelog

This is the full list of user-facing changes to sage, newest first. The README has no list of changes: it links here.
Each date is the day of the first commit that made the change. Older changes are in the [git log](https://github.com/erickb336/sage/commits/main). In these entries, "the sage" is the chief, the main session in sage mode.

> **Warning:** before you use waits or programs, update sage and restart every session that was already open. An older session still merges a waiting task, or a task of a program that you did not approve. See [To update sage](docs/guide/using-sage.md#to-update-sage).

## 2026-11-04

- **The last two move fixes before any real move (T648).** Fixes from the reviews of T647.
  - A command that waited on an old logbook's lock refuses while a move plan names that logbook, also when its root is another path to the same folder: through a link, or in another letter case on a volume that ignores case. Before, it wrote into the unmarked old logbook, and the move could not finish.
    - The path rule: two folders that exist compare by device and inode (`sameDir`), which every path to a folder shares. A folder that is gone compares by its path, as before.
    - Why not a realpath: Node's `realpathSync` resolves links but keeps the letter case that it was given. `realpathSync.native` gives the case on disk on macOS, but that depends on the system, and a case fold would need a test of the volume. The inode needs neither.
    - Why not the folder name: the new shared logbook has the same folder name as the old logbook that holds the move gate, so a match by name would also refuse the new logbook.
    - The same rule now also covers the move's own check for a stopped plan and the resolver's check before the lock.
    - A path in a plan that is missing or is no valid name (a NUL byte, a name too long) names no folder, so it is not this logbook. Before, it gave a raw error to every writer of every project.
    - A path in a plan that the system cannot read for any other reason (no right to search a folder on the way, a link loop, a disk error) may be another path to this logbook. So the command refuses, names the path and the error, and changes nothing. This also stops the writers of other projects until the owner fixes the rights or the plan.
  - A move that stopped finishes from the other provider also when that provider's roots are other paths to the same folders. Before, the finish refused and told the owner to check the plan file.
  - A round key whose finding closed before the move keeps its new key also after the next round. The move writes one decision row for each such key, with the key as its first word, so the key counter counts it. Before, the next round dropped the key, and a new finding of the task took it again, so the decision trail had one key for two findings.
    - A repair that accepts the loss of the decisions writes one row again for each round key with no finding (`F-T4-2 is a round key of T4 with no finding`), so the key stays taken after that repair too.
- **The move's recovery paths and edge cases (T647), before any real move.** Fixes from the reviews of the move (T640).
  - A move gate moves once. After a restore by hand, its answer moves nothing: the move wrote a row in the gate's logbook, and the restored folder keeps the plan in its name. The owner answers a new preview and gate.
  - The restore steps end with a seventh step: rename the plan `moves/<folder>.json` to `<folder>.json.aside` when it is there, so that a project with an end check that did not match is not blocked after a restore.
  - The move writes the highest new number of its map into each old logbook's decisions, so after a restore no new task, gate or program takes a number of the map.
  - The end check splits the standing orders only at the headings that the move writes, so an owner's own heading that starts with "## From the " no longer fails a move.
  - A program moves whole: its finished tasks, also a merged pilot, move with it as finished tasks with new numbers, so its pilot, its breakdown approval and its done count stay. The move no longer refuses a program whose pilot merged.
  - A round key whose finding closed before the move moves as a new key with no row, so the task's next round counts as before the move and does not go to replan.
  - A chain of adoptions gives each old row the number of the task that moves at its end; a loop of adoptions refuses.
  - A command that found an old logbook and waited on its lock refuses while a move plan names that logbook, so a stop between the marks of two old logbooks still finishes with the same command.
- **A new project starts in a shared logbook (T642, PR 7c of the shared logbook).** `sage init` of a project with no logbook links it with `sage link --separate` when every plugin is ready, and says so: "<checkout> now uses the shared logbook <folder>. Every plugin is ready, so the project starts there."
  - Ready: each provider root has its provider's name, `plugins.tsv` has each provider at contract 2 or recorded as unused, and neither provider root has a logbook of this repository, also a clone's (rule 2 wins, so that one move later takes them together).
  - Otherwise `init` makes a legacy logbook, as before, with no new text. An explicit `SAGE_HOME` stands for every root, so a scratch run keeps a legacy logbook. A `plugins.tsv` that sage cannot read is not ready.
  - A checkout with the first commit of a shared logbook still gets the link prompt, and a repository with no commit yet starts shared: its row gets the first commit at a later write.
  - Only the move gate records a provider as unused.

## 2026-11-03

- **Safe ground for the move of existing logbooks (T641, PR 7a of the shared logbook).** Nothing moves yet: every command of a legacy or a shared logbook works as before.
  - A logbook with a `moved.json` marker refuses every write under its lock, with a line that says it moved and to run the command again, which then finds the shared logbook. So a writer that found the old logbook just before the move and waited on its lock writes nothing there. A read still reads it.
  - The move can write one id floor row per prefix (T, R, G and PG) in the new logbook's decisions, for example `T644 is the task floor of the move from claude and codex`. Every sage, also an older one, then gives the next number above it, so an id of an old logbook never comes back. A finding's key counts inside its task, so it needs no floor.
  - The plugin contract in `plugins.tsv` is now 2: a state tool that writes 2 refuses a moved logbook. The move can ask which providers still wait: a provider with no row, or below 2, waits; a row with `unused` does not.
  - An adoption record of version 2 reads: the PR and the branch are optional, and `from` keeps the task's own version 1 record, so an adopted task's branch and PR stay its own after the move. A version 1 record reads as before.
  - The Claude plugin names the provider of each old logbook root. A plugin that gives a bare path still works, with no provider name.
- **The move of an existing project into one shared logbook (T640, PR 7b of the shared logbook).** Tell either chief to move the project: it shows a preview that changes nothing, then one gate.
  - `sage move --preview` prints what moves by provider, with the new numbers (Claude's first), what stays, the next numbers, the checks and the plan, a fingerprint of everything that the move writes. It refuses, with nothing changed, while a run runs, while a provider's plugin is below contract 2, and when a folder cannot be written.
  - `sage move --plan <plan>` opens the move gate. A provider with no row in `plugins.tsv` gets "move, and record it as unused" in place of "move". The preview and the gate name each other checkout that the move links, by path. A move gate answers once.
  - `sage move --gate <G>` moves after your answer: it checks the plan again under the locks, saves it, builds the new logbook, marks the old logbooks (with a backup copy of each task table), links the checkouts, counts each table by provider against the plan, and then removes the plan. A plan that no longer matches moves nothing and says what changed.
  - A move that stops: every command of the project, in Claude and in Codex, and a link, refuses and names the same command, which finishes it from any checkout of the move. A saved plan that names a folder, a logbook or a checkout that is not this repository's refuses. An end check that does not match names each missing record and the steps to set the plan aside, and no command.
  - The open tasks keep their branch and PR through adoption version 2, their findings, gates, programs and waits move with new numbers (also those of a task that they adopted, and the task numbers in a gate's question), and finished tasks, runs, verdicts and kept reports stay in the old logbooks, read-only. Codex's standing orders follow Claude's under a heading, with their lines that have no number.
  - On the board, a moved card shows its old number, for example `was Claude T640`, for the life of the task, and a banner names the move and its map page for 7 days. The restore steps end with a rename of the new logbook's folder to a dot name, so that no task shows twice.
  - A moved gate's question maps each finding key through the move, through the gate's own task first, so a move approval names the same finding; each task's round keys name its own findings, also when two tasks have the same key. A finished task with an open gate refuses the preview, which lists each such gate. A resumed plan must name the old logbook that holds its answered move gate. The move's local times carry their zone (`UTC+05:30`), and the restore step's dot name holds the plan.
  - A repair of a moved logbook's decisions writes the move's id floors again. The Codex `move` tool comes with the Codex part of the move.
- **The PR script and the Claude hook read a shared task's branch in its writer's clone (T634, PR 6a of the shared logbook).** In a shared logbook with two clones that `sage link --to` linked, the branch lives in the checkout of the branch's newest writer run (implementer, designer or arena judge), not always in the chief's folder. A legacy logbook does not change.
  - `sage-pr` reads the origin of that checkout, so a chief in clone B pushes and opens the pull request on the repository of clone A, where the implementer worked.
  - One logbook has one repository: when that checkout's origin is another GitHub repository than the origin of the logbook's owner checkout, `sage-pr` refuses (exit 1), names the two repositories and pushes nothing.
  - When that checkout is gone, `sage-pr` refuses (exit 1) with the run's ID, pushes nothing and changes no table. Start the run again from a live checkout.
  - A writer run from before T625 has no checkout, so `sage-pr` reads the chief's own folder, as before.
  - The Claude hook reads a task branch's tip in the same checkout, for example the commit that a review's report keeps. A gone checkout gives no commit, so that report backs no verdict.
- **Linked clones show as one project on the board, and the chief asks before each link (T633, PR 6b of the shared logbook).** A shared logbook with two or more linked checkouts is one project. A project with one checkout, and a legacy logbook, do not change.
  - The project picker's second line names the live checkouts in link order, for example `sample-owner/lantern · 2 checkouts: lantern, lantern-b`. A gone checkout does not count.
  - Two checkouts with one folder name show `lantern #1` and `lantern #2`, by link order, in the picker and on their runs. A number never moves to another folder. No page shows a checkout's path.
  - A row of `bindings.tsv` that links a folder to another project's logbook is one line in the board's Logbook notes, by its folder name.
  - "Show board" in a clone with no row no longer shows a shared project of the same folder name as if it were linked.
  - When a command stops in a new clone or in a folder with a wrong link, the chief asks you one choice, link or start separate, with a recommendation, and runs [`sage link`](docs/guide/using-sage.md#shared-logbooks) only after your answer.
  - The state tool's refusal holds the whole prompt, so the chief asks it word for word in both providers: the warning that no sage command can change the answer later, the numbered choices with the command of each, and the recommendation by GitHub remote (the same remote: link; another remote, a fork: separate; no remote: link). A row that names a missing logbook offers to restore it first.
  - The guide says that a shallow clone, or a clone whose first commit Git cannot read, gets a legacy logbook at `init`, which a later link refuses (T610).
- **The board reads old logbooks and `sources.tsv` more safely (T630, before the move of existing projects).** The [board guide](docs/guide/board.md#a-shared-project-on-the-board) has the lines.
  - A `sources.tsv` row that the board does not read is now a line under Logbook notes, not an incomplete source: the board page stays live for every project. A folder that the board cannot search, or a folder name that is too long, refuses only its own row. Only the provider words `claude` and `codex` read.
  - An open gate on a finished old task is not in Needs you. An open row that a move did not finish says that it is open, not finished.
  - The task view of a shared logbook in a session finds an old finished task by its id.
  - A shared root that is a link or a file is one quiet note for a project that is not shared, not a lasting incomplete source.
  - A board source of another id at the shared root's path reads as the shared root.
  - A run's checkout folder name on the task page loses bidi and control characters. A folder past the 64 that the board checks says `· not checked`. A checkout that is now a plain file or an empty folder is gone: the review refuses with the run's ID, and readiness gives `readiness-checkout`.
- **Each run of a shared logbook saves its checkout (T625, PR 5b of the shared logbook).** In Claude and in Codex, a new run of a shared logbook records the main checkout of the folder that it started from, in a new `checkout` column of `runs.tsv`. A legacy logbook does not change: it gets no column. The [board guide](docs/guide/board.md#a-shared-project-on-the-board) has the lines.
  - A shared task's page shows `checkout <folder>` under each run's role: the folder name only, never its path. The chat text adds ` · checkout <folder>` after the role. A run from before this change shows no line.
  - When that folder is not on this Mac now, the run shows `· gone`. While the task is active, one note under the runs says that its next review step stops until the folder is back.
  - In Codex, a review reads the task branch in the checkout of the branch's newest writer run (implementer, designer or arena judge), so a second clone that `sage link --to` linked reads the right commit. That checkout must be a row of `bindings.tsv` for the logbook. A gone checkout refuses with the run's ID and changes nothing; a move to verified gives the code `readiness-checkout`. Start the run again from a live checkout.
  - **Update the sage plugin in Claude and in Codex.** After the first run add of this version, a sage from before it refuses every write to that shared logbook, and the Codex review capture, because `runs.tsv` has a column that it does not know. Reads still work.
- **The board shows a shared project (T624, PR 5a of the shared logbook).** In Claude and in Codex, the chat board and the board page show a project with a shared logbook as one project. The board only reads. An existing project looks as before. The [board guide](docs/guide/board.md#a-shared-project-on-the-board) has each line.
  - The board reads the shared root beside the Claude and Codex roots. A new board config lists it. An existing config does not change: the server and each board command add the shared root when they read.
  - A shared logbook has no `checkout.txt`, so the board takes the checkout from its row in `bindings.tsv`, by the state tool's own owner rule. The project's name and its PR links come from that checkout.
  - Each shared card names its owning chief (`Claude · C1`), or `Unclaimed` with a dashed outline, and an open offer: it waits for a run to end, or the chief can accept now. The Who filter goes by the owning chief's provider, and an unclaimed task shows only under All.
  - A shared task's page has a Provider column in its runs, from each run's chief in `chiefs.tsv`. sage writes no new column for it.
  - Needs you asks an open Replace gate in one line. A running run of the owning chief with no change for over 24 h puts the task in Needs you: its chief may have stopped (the default of gate G103).
  - The finished tasks of the old logbooks that `sources.tsv` names show in Done with `Old · Claude · read-only` or `Old · Codex · read-only`. A moved row is hidden. The board reads only a folder with `moved.json` under a root of the row's provider, by the same rule in the chat and on the board page. A program that moved shows only in the shared logbook; an old logbook shows only its finished programs, never in Needs you. Only the move (a later PR) writes these files.
  - A task whose chief id is not in `chiefs.tsv` says so on its own page, not as a setting that the board ignores.
  - A run of a shared logbook joins its agent slot in its provider's root, so a Claude run no longer shows as "may be stuck" on the Agents page.
  - The board reads a logbook again when it changed during the read, at most 3 times. Then the note "The logbook is changing" shows over the last good read on the board page, and over the third read in the chat. When a part of the third read changed while the board read it, the note names that part in plain words: the whole logbook, a table such as `tasks.tsv`, or an artifact.
  - The chief's text names `sage board all --view chat` for "show board".
  - After you update sage in Claude and in Codex, stop a running board server with the `board --stop` command that `board --ensure` prints, then ask for the board again.
- **Truer lines for chiefs on a shared logbook.** Each refusal and success line of a transfer now says what happened and the next step (T617). The [usage guide](docs/guide/using-sage.md#shared-logbooks) has the tables.
  - Your answer keep, or your own words, to a replace gate now prints `nothing replaced`: the task keeps its chief, no run ended, and the gate is spent. Before, the line looked like a success, so a chief could report a replacement that did not happen.
  - The chief that an offer names can decline it: it runs `cancel` with the offer's id. The offer clears, the line says that the recipient declined, and the owning chief keeps the task. Before, the recipient got a refusal that pointed to a Replace gate.
  - `projects rebuild` is your act, as `logbook repair` is, so the line that sage prints works in your terminal on a shared logbook.
  - In Claude, a `gh pr merge` event with no session id no longer skips the owner rule of a shared logbook: the merge check refuses it.
  - An ended task (merged, concluded or abandoned) of another chief on the same commit no longer bars a live task's merge.
  - A lead that meets another chief's task, or a task with no owning chief, is told to report to its chief, not to claim or open a gate.
  - A write with no chief no longer says that a hook names the id where no hook runs. An accept or a release that waits for a run names the Replace gate too, because a run of unknown status may never end.
  - The verdict refusal counts the rows of the run by severity, and its line to record a finding has `--key`, so a retry adds no second row. A stuck saved change with a damaged `decisions.tsv` prints one repair line, not two.
  - The Codex `accept` tool names `sage_read_task` for the offer's id and the version, and the `cancel` tool names the decline.

## 2026-11-02

- **Fewer false refusals from the hook.** Three hook rules stopped harmless work, and a real write to the logbook is still refused (T621).
  - The rule for a logbook write drops a plain reader from a Bash command line. So `touch a && ls <logbook folder>` passes, and a pattern or a name in a reader that only redirects (`jq '.items[]' a.json > /tmp/out`) passes. Every other part stays judged, also one that the hook does not know. A line with a substitution, a group, control flow, an alias, an assignment or a `>!` is judged whole, and so is every line of another tool, such as PowerShell.
  - The hook reads the run from a brief's first line that ends with punctuation, such as `Run R7 · task T3: build`. The refusal for an agent with no run names each cause.
  - An implementer can run `gh pr create` and the other allowed `gh` commands after `cd <worktree>` and `git push`, and it can give the value of `--body` or `--title` of `gh pr` as `"$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`, in double quotes. Before, only one plain `gh` command passed.
  - A blank GitHub repository has a way forward. The first push makes the task's branch the default branch, and then the push rule refused that branch. The main session can now run `gh repo edit github.com/<owner>/<repo> --default-branch main`, which asks you and shows what GitHub counts. The hook first checks on GitHub that main is one root commit, and it refuses past 20 commits on the default branch, 5 branches or 3 open pull requests. No agent gets this form, and no agent pushes to main.
- **Hand a task to another chief on a shared logbook.** One chief can hand a task to another chief or give it up. With your answer, a chief can take over from a chief that stopped (T618). The [usage guide](docs/guide/using-sage.md#shared-logbooks) has the table.
  - `offer` names one other chief. The owning chief stays until that chief runs `accept`, with the exact offer, the current version and no active or unknown run. `cancel` clears the offer, and a cancelled offer never becomes valid.
  - `release` clears the owning chief, so any chief can `claim` the task.
  - `gate replace` opens a gate for you. Your answer replace sets the chief, clears an open offer and ends each run that the gate names as failed, in one saved change. The next write of any chief finishes it after a stop. This is also the way out for a Claude session after `/clear`, which is a new chief.
  - The gate's question names the title, both chiefs with their providers and each run with its role, and it says what each answer does. Only your answer counts: this rule is an instruction, not a check.
  - A replaced chief gets a refusal that names the new owning chief, also for `sage-pr create` and `sage-pr merge`, for `gh pr merge` in Claude and in Codex, and for a Codex review that it accepts. A run that ends does not advance a transfer, and a transfer changes no run.
  - A run that ended as blocked or failed keeps a late report once, with its arrival time. `task <T>` prints its path, and that report backs no verdict.
  - A Codex chief has the tools `offer`, `cancel`, `accept`, `release` and `gate_replace`, with the same rules.
  - An existing project shows no change: only a shared logbook has these commands, the `offer` column and the gate `kind` column.
- **A candidate run stays off another task's branch.** `run add` now refuses a candidate run on a branch that another task names by its `branch=`, or where a writer run of another task worked, in any letter case, also after that run ended. The refusal names that task and says to use another branch. Before, the run went in, and its row then barred the other task from its own branch for good. The Claude and Codex paths share the rule. A review run claims no branch, and a build on a branch that two tasks share works as before. A candidate run stays off a shared branch too, because a candidate's branch never lands.
- **A helper's slot stays held until the helper really stops.** When the sage ends a helper's run while the helper still runs, the run ends in the logbook and the lead goes on, but the helper's slot stays held, so the agent cap counts the helper. The helper's own stop frees the slot. Its report then counts in the lead's check for unrecorded findings, and the ended run keeps its status. If no stop comes, the one-hour lease frees the slot. So after a restart, the slot of a helper that died holds for up to an hour after the sage's `run done`. Before, `run done` freed the slot at once, and the late report was lost.
- **A moved or dismissed finding no longer needs an empty commit.** Before, a `findings` or `qa-fail` verdict refused its commit for good, also after triage moved or dismissed each of its findings. Now the merge check and the move to verified pass over such a verdict when its run links it to at least one finding, and each finding of that run is moved, or dismissed below high. A verdict with no link, an open finding, a finding closed as fixed, a dismissed high finding, or a moved finding back on the task still refuses, and a `checks-fail` verdict always does. So that a part of a bad report cannot clear it, a `findings` or `qa-fail` verdict now needs each medium and high finding of its run's report on record for that run, and a closed finding is no longer dismissed. A cleared verdict never counts as clean: the commit still needs its full clean cycles. The board no longer shows "QA failed" for a commit that passes the merge check (T294).

## 2026-11-01

- **The lead limit is now a config key.** `max_leads` sets the most running leads of a project, and its default is 5 (it was a fixed 3). Ask the chief in the chat, and it runs `sage config max_leads=<n>`. The state tool and the hook read the same value. A lower value ends no lead: it only refuses the next one. The agent caps still apply to each lead.
- **Each default root now reads the HOME of the env it gets.** A caller that gives the state tool or the Codex mode hook an env with a scratch HOME, and no SAGE_HOME, now stays under that HOME. Before, these roots read the process's own home folder, so such a run could write to the real sage root. Sessions and commands do not change: their env is the process's env, so they find the same root as before.
- **The repair of a stuck logbook now gives a true next step in two more cases.** A task-update receipt of a newer schema now gets the plugin update line, not the backup line. With a damaged receipt in `interrupted-runs`, the repair now goes on and warns that a later Codex settle may stop on that receipt; before, the repair said that writes work. The pages folder also follows the HOME of the env that a caller gives, so a scratch HOME stays in scratch, and an empty HOME or SAGE_WORKTREES never gives a relative path. Sessions and commands find the same folder as before (T607).
- **Chiefs and one guard for a shared logbook.** Two chiefs on one shared logbook can no longer overwrite each other's task (T604).
  - `chiefs.tsv` names each chief of the logbook. A resume keeps its session, so it is the same chief. Claude's `/clear` starts a new chief.
  - `task add` gives the task to the chief that adds it. The `chief` column of `tasks.tsv` and `runs.tsv` names it, and `claim` takes a task with no owning chief.
  - A write on a task of another chief refuses and names the owning chief. A lead acts for the chief of its lead run, on that task only. A command with no chief only reads.
  - A Claude chief adds `--chief C<n>`, and a Claude lead adds `--lead R<n>`; the hook names the id, also on a write with a quoted value. A Codex chief or lead adds nothing, and Codex has a `claim` tool.
  - The CLI, the Codex tools and the native tools `sage_update_task` and `sage_create_run` give the same refusal: it names the owning chief, or the version to claim, in the form that the reader's provider can use. A Codex tool also gives the real cause of a refusal, such as a damaged `chiefs.tsv` or a busy lock.
  - Each form of `logbook repair` is the owner's act and names no chief, so the line that a refusal prints works in the owner's terminal. The design's table had both forms under any chief.
  - An existing project shows no change: only a shared logbook has this file and this column. An older sage refuses to write a shared logbook that has the column.
- **Codex text fixes from the role pilot.** sage on Codex now states one rule: it needs a multi-agent v2 model for the chief and each child. On a v1 session, the chief starts no agents and tells you to start a new session on a v2 model; the earlier v1 path, which could not finish a task, is gone. The chief no longer starts a fresh lead after a lead reports that it has no spawn tools. The chief and a lead now stay in their turn while a child runs, because a child's report starts no turn, and the chief's last line says what to send if it stops all the same. The implementer, designer, arena judge and lead now know that git writes and network steps ask you for approval, and that a sandbox refusal is not a failed task. QA, the reviewers, the PE and the investigation roles get a short rule: a sandbox refusal is not a failed check or a finding, so they run the command again with escalation. The chief has the same rule for `gh pr view` and `gh pr checks`, and the guide's prompt table lists them. The guide's "What you need" now lists the v2 model. After a refused `git worktree add -b`, an agent checks for a branch that the failed step left, and then does not use `-b` again. The guide gives the count (at least 5 in each small task). It says that `writable_roots` with the network is not proved, and it lists the escalated push under a strict sandbox as not proved. The text names the real limit message, `collab spawn failed: agent thread limit reached`, and says how `wait_agent` works. The tested Codex range now ends at 0.166.
- **A lead moves on from a fix that the re-check does not confirm.** `round` now also starts from repairing, so a lead triages the repeat fix, runs `round` on its own task, and goes on with the next round. Before, the task sat at repairing until the chief moved it and ran `round` by hand. The round limit, the hold after the last round, your gate for a round past the limit and the replan of a round that fixed none of its keys stay as they were. A lead still ends blocked for a new finding of a re-check, and for a low key with no medium or high finding open.
- **A moved or re-cloned checkout gets a true next step (T599).** A checkout with no row and a shared logbook's first commit no longer starts a logbook.
  - Each command and `init` refuse, name the logbook, and offer `sage link --to <folder>` or `sage link --separate`. Before, `init` made a logbook that the link then refused.
  - A row of a checkout that left the disk no longer refuses the only live checkout. It can still keep out a checkout with other first commits.
  - A `--to` with a wrong folder lists the logbooks in the refusal, so a Codex chief needs no read of `projects.tsv`.
  - A command from a folder that is gone says so and names the next step.
- **A shared root for logbooks, and link commands.** The shared root is `~/.sage`. It holds the logbooks that Claude and Codex share (T594).
  - `sage link --separate` makes a new logbook in the shared root. `sage link --to <folder>` joins a checkout to a logbook there. Codex has a `link` tool.
  - The chief runs a link only after your answer. A row in `bindings.tsv` then gives Claude and Codex the same logbook and the same cycle counts.
  - An existing project has no row and shows no change. A new project still starts in its provider's logbook.
  - A link refuses a project that has a logbook. Only the move, in a later pull request, takes its tasks over.
  - Both hooks protect the shared root. The board does not show a shared logbook yet.
- **A saved change that cannot finish now has a way out with no backup.** When you accept the loss, the chief runs `sage logbook repair --accept-change-loss yes`. The repair records a decision, keeps the stuck file as `review-pending.json.lost-<n>`, and the project saves again. It refuses, and changes nothing, on a logbook with no saved change, on a change that can finish, on a change that may finish from the real folder of a logbook behind a link or on a newer sage, and on a damaged task-update receipt, which needs a backup. It does not repair the tables, and it says so: a half-published update can leave mixed tables, and tables that are each whole but do not agree pass the logbook check. Sage still never drops a saved change by itself; this step needs your answer each time. A shared logbook takes the same repair from any checkout that is linked to it; a shared root behind a link refuses as above, and the line names `SAGE_SHARED_HOME`. In Codex, no tool runs the repair, so you run it in a terminal (T593).
- **The arena's rules and the chief's arena text now agree, so the Codex arena pilot can run on them.** An abandoned task has no open arena step, so the abandon exit of an open step no longer ends in a second refusal on the same commit; a candidate's branch still never merges, also for an abandoned task. An investigation with an arena no longer concludes while its arena step is open: the move to concluded refuses with the same exits as the other refusals. `--add arena` on a tiny task now also adds the code review, because a judge's graft is new code that nobody read, and a build route with no code review takes no arena candidate. The task's cycles follow from its route: one clean cycle of that review, with no QA, and its lead adds only the review and QA roles of its route. The chief's arena steps now say that a large task before briefed takes only designers, that a candidate run opens the step on a task with no arena block, and that the chief shows you the judge's scores, base, grafts, rejections and empty candidates after a judge ends done.
- **A Codex chief can now run an arena, in the same order as in Claude Code.** You ask the Codex chief for an arena, as for any other request. The chief records the rubric, starts up to three candidates at one time, each on its own branch, then starts the arena judge and goes on to the reviews or the PE. A candidate's or a judge's run on a branch of its own task now passes the native run check, and a reviewer's run stays on the task's branch. A Codex judge leaves the pull request to the chief, and its role text now says so. A native move that an open arena refuses now names the judge as the way out. A tiny arena that an older sage saved no longer reads as damaged after an update: a retry or a stopped write settles it with the route that it was saved with. A synthetic test plays the flow; the first real run is the installed pilot, after this change. The guides, the task's life graphic and its alt text now say that a tiny arena has the code review.
- **A stopped write no longer needs the chief that started it.** If a logbook write stops half way, the next write from Claude or Codex finishes it or undoes it. A write that cannot finish stops its own project, and other projects still merge, with two limits that fail closed: a marker that sage cannot read refuses every merge, and a stuck project with a ledger row for a commit refuses the merge of that commit in any project. Update sage in Claude and Codex together, because an older sage refuses the new record that Codex now writes. A write that cannot finish reads the same short line in Claude and in Codex, and that line tells the owner how to restore the folder from a backup. One more limit: the merge check searches a saved change for the commit as text, so a note that quotes the commit also stops the merge until a write in that project finishes the change or says what to do. It fails closed (T578).
- **A Codex chief now starts one lead for each task with a build.** The chief records the lead run and starts `sage_lead_t<n>_r<k>`, with the role text first in the message. `role.mjs lead` now prints the Codex steps: how a lead starts each helper, waits, reads a report, records its task in the order that the tools need, opens the pull request and steers its team by a new agent. On multi-agent v1 the chief does the lead's work, as before. When Codex returns `AgentLimitReached`, the role texts say what to do. The refusal of a lead's message now gives the right reason and step: a lead starts a new agent on a new run. The warning after a spawn with no checked brief now tells a lead to stop the agent with `interrupt_agent`, the stop tool of multi-agent v2. The gate now also runs for `resume_agent`, so a role agent cannot restart a closed agent, and a lead gets its own refusal with the same step. The guide names a lead's exceptions, the refusal of a bad chain of agent names and the new limits. No real Codex run has checked a lead yet.
- **A Codex lead can now record its own task.** A child of the chief named `sage_lead_t<n>`, while its task's lead run runs, may use the sage tools for runs, findings, verdicts, rounds, pages and briefs of its own task, and move that task through a cycle. Each call on another task is refused with a line that names the rule. The rules follow the Claude lead's: a lead adds only runs of its team, dismisses only a low finding, moves no finding to another task, leaves a checks verdict to the chief, repairs through a round, and closes each fix of the round before it goes back to reviewing. A lead whose lead run ended, or whose task is held or finished, records nothing and starts no agent. A reviewer or QA agent under a lead now has its report kept, so that it can back a verdict. The gate's proof of a call now carries the caller, and the sage server applies the caller's rule itself. Only the session's main thread passes as the chief, whatever name a child has. The chief still starts no lead in Codex, so nothing changes for you yet.
- **The Codex gate now lets a lead start its own team.** A child named `sage_lead_t<n>` may start implementer, code reviewer, security reviewer, UX reviewer and QA agents with the same task number. The gate refuses any other spawn by a lead, with a line that names the rule. Under a lead, the last sage name of the agent path decides the edit rule: an implementer edits, a reviewer or QA stays read-only, and the lead itself edits nothing. A path with any other sage name above the last one is refused. Sends stay refused. The chief still starts no lead in Codex, so nothing changes for you yet.
- **The Codex report check now refuses each report that the Claude stop gate refuses.** The reader was already in core, and T560 connected it for a review child with a run in its task name. Two differences stayed. A review or QA child with no run in its name, or with another letter case, got the field check only: a report with a high finding that the reader cannot read went through. Codex also had its own field rule, so a field in a list item, on an indented line or in a code block counted. Now the reader follows the role in the task name, and the one field rule (`missingFields`) moved from the Claude hook into core, in place of the Codex rule. The Codex guide no longer says that the check does not read a review's findings (T461).
- **The board keeps up with a write that macOS does not report.** On macOS each new file watch restarts the file event stream, and a write in that time gave no event, so the board could stay out of date until the next change. On a busy Mac this also failed the board server tests with "no matching board event". The board now reads the logbooks five times in the 15 seconds after a new watch, not once. You do not need to do anything.

## 2026-10-31

- **Codex keeps each arena report, and a candidate's report names the commit of its own branch.** The report check now keeps the exact report of an implementer and of an arena judge, so `report_compare` finds them. Before, it returned `missing`. No verdict depends on these reports. A writer run (an implementer, an arena judge or a designer) gets the head of its own branch at its stop, also when it committed during the run. A missing branch gives no commit, and the check never uses the task's branch instead. A review or QA run reads the branch of its task, and that branch must not move during the run, or the run gets no commit.
- **The arena's shared rules are now in the state tool, for both providers.** An arena judge now works on its own new branch: its run needs `--branch`, the chief names that branch at `run add` (for example `sage/t12-judge`), and the judge makes it from the chosen candidate's head and stops if it exists. For a build, the judge opens a draft pull request from that branch, and a lead takes it through the reviews and QA. For a design, the PE checks it, you approve it, and the build starts on a new branch from main. When the candidates diverge on the product, the judge reports both choices with a recommendation, the chief asks you, and a new judge run goes on with your answer. A branch has one writer, a judge too, and a branch name in another letter case counts as the same branch. A task's arena step is open while its route has the arena block or it has a candidate run, and no judge of it ended done. While it is open, an implementer or designer run needs `--candidate`, a whole number, and the move to verified, the merge check and `sage-pr create` refuse the task and name the way out: finish a judge, or for a task that needs no arena, abandon it and frame it again. An arena on a large task is a design arena, with the order arena, PE, your approval, build, and the judge saves the final design as a page for you to approve. A build arena runs only on a tiny or small task, or after an approved design. The state tool refuses a judge on a candidate's branch, a candidate on a judge's branch and any other writer on a candidate's branch, in both orders, also after a run ended. The move to verified, the merge check and `sage-pr create` now refuse a candidate's branch, by the pull request's head branch or, with no `--head`, by the task's `branch=`, and a task with candidates and no branch named. The rule reads the branch, not the commit, so a judge with no graft lands the candidate's commit from its own branch. Each candidate commits its artifact, saves a copy in the pages folder and opens no pull request, and the chief records the copy with `pages`. Candidate branches and pages stay until the owner deletes them, a merge deletes the branch that it lands, and worktrees go at the end of the task. Update sage before you start an arena: a judge that an older chief starts with no branch is refused, and an arena that runs during the update must finish on a new judge branch.
- **A lead's foreground helpers keep their reports.** The lead's Agent tool can return only when the helper ends, so the call's result comes after the helper's stop. The hook now joins a lead's helper to its run at the helper's start, when its call is the only pending one of its role in the session. So the report is kept at the stop, the lead's verdict with that run passes, and the helper has its scratch folder during its work. Two pending calls of one role stay unjoined, because no start event names its call: each such run keeps no report, and it ends as failed. A brief's first line, `Run R<n> · task T<n>`, now also gives a helper's run. It must name the lead's own task, and it must agree with a name that is a run id. The other lead rules did not change. An Agent call that fails after its helper started now frees the slot, and the run may get a new helper.
- **The inactive Codex turn-trigger observer always ends inside its 1.8 s deadline with one fixed answer.** The reader now runs in a child process. At the deadline the command kills the child and leaves, so a stalled disk read no longer holds the command open. A failed start of the reader returns `file_unavailable` instead of a stack trace. A run through a linked path now prints its answer instead of nothing. Every existing bound and refusal stays. No manifest calls the observer (T580).
- **Adoption works when task numbers overlap across providers.** A branch such as `codex/t95-init-lock-test` no longer counts as claimed by an unrelated destination T95. Only a recorded claim refuses adoption: a task's PR history, its recorded branch or a run on that branch. After adoption, the merge check, `sage-pr` and the lead's branch rule treat the adopted branch as the adopted task's own. Source claims, provenance, spent rounds and fresh destination reviews do not change (T575).
- **A backed verdict on the first try, for a review or QA that the chief starts itself.** The chief's instructions now say that the brief of such a review or QA starts with the line `Run R<n> · task T<n> (...)`, and that the Claude hook keeps the report for the run only by that line. The Codex report check now reads a review or QA child's report at its first stop, as the Claude stop gate does: a report that it cannot read blocks once with the reason, and the second stop keeps it. The note for T483 said that the report's commit is "each full SHA in its BRANCH". The state tool takes the one full SHA, or the one after the word head when BRANCH names more; the design page now says so (T560).
- **A warning when autopilot runs without branch protection.** When autopilot turns on, sage reads once per session (read-only `gh` checks, all inside one 5 second limit) whether the default branch of the repository requires a pull request, through a ruleset or a branch protection rule. If not, the confirmation adds one line with the steps to turn it on. A private repository on a free GitHub plan gets a different line: GitHub offers no protection there, so the line says to make the repository public or upgrade to GitHub Pro. Autopilot still runs and lands as before, and a failed or slow read says "could not check" and blocks nothing. Claude Code and Codex both do this (T547).

A folder with no `.git` inside another repository no longer gets the merge base of that repository. The chief's steps in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) now give the commands: `git fetch origin main`, `git switch -c <branch> origin/main` and `git merge origin/main` (T559).

On a change-log branch, undo the edit from `origin/main`, run `npm run changelog`, and put the text in a task pull request. The refusal of a task diff that edits `CHANGELOG.md` puts `git fetch origin main` before the `git checkout`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has one part for an implementer and one for the chief, and says to merge main into a stale change-log branch first. The chief's instructions name the change-log pull request after task pull requests merge (T542).

The gate also refuses a shell write to Codex's config file (the hook trust) or to the sage plugin's folder. - **Two pull requests no longer conflict in the change log.** A pull request now carries only its own `changes/<task>.md`, and `npm run build` no longer writes `CHANGELOG.md`. A push to a remote with any name passes for the task's branch, so a project whose one remote is `github` works. A push to main, master or the default branch is refused in every form: `HEAD:main`, `:main`, `refs/heads/main`, `--all`, `--mirror`, a URL, `-C`, `git -c`, a symbolic branch ref, and the settings `remote.<name>.push`, `remote.<name>.mirror`, `url.<base>.insteadOf` and `push.default` upstream. Beside the push, a line may only run `cd <dir>` (no option, and no `||` or `&` in the line), `pwd`, `git add`, `commit`, `status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `fetch` or `rev-parse`, `gh`, `echo`, `printf`, `true`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `grep` or `wc`, and writes no file (`tee` or `>` is refused) and sets no upstream (`--set-upstream`, fetch's `-u`). `git subtree push`, a git subcommand that is not a known built-in (`send-pack`, an alias), a setting of `core.hooksPath` or `core.fsmonitor` (by `git config`, `git -c`, `--config-env`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` or `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, also inside `sh -c`), a write under `.git` (also by git's own `--prefix`, `--output` or `-o`), `gh repo sync`, `gh repo edit --default-branch` and a `gh api` write of `default_branch` are refused too, also with a doubled or trailing slash in the route. When the board does not know the last commit, the card says that the merge check is not checked. The board does not see the pull request's head branch on GitHub, so it says that this part is not checked (T280).
- **Verify installed Codex package files.** The chief and assigned roles can run `sage.mjs verify-install --commit <full40hexSHA> --project <absolute assigned project>`. It compares tracked package files with that commit, reports counts and relative paths, and writes nothing. Project identity and object reads ignore inherited Git selectors and use trusted system Git locations independently of `PATH`. Missing local objects fail without remote access or repository transport helpers. Regular-file entries must reference actual blobs, not tags that point to matching bytes. This check does not establish runtime trust or release readiness. Installation and configuration writes remain blocked.
- **Scoped Codex role reads.** Role agents can read a task, its task board and configuration for the project in Codex's hook context. These reads do not initialize or rewrite logbook files. Commands require literal arguments and absolute interpreter and CLI paths. Task boards read and judge only the assigned logbook. A passing project check gives no merge approval; the chief's merge check still covers all logbooks. Other projects, providers, command wrappers and state writes stay refused.
- **Approve one more repair round.** A round hold now needs an explicit, task-specific owner approval. It permits one round above the spent rounds or current limit, whichever is greater. Adopted tasks keep their spent rounds and pull request. Reused approvals grant nothing; earlier allowances and review requirements remain. Native task creation, review acceptance, title changes and round resumes saved before an upgrade retain their saved rules, bytes and hashes. They can recover after an interruption; new resumes still require an unused approval.
- **Adopt an existing task and PR across providers.** The chief can use `task_adopt` in Codex, or `task-adopt` in the state CLI. Sage checks the project, source task, PR and live head branch. Another task's recorded run on the branch also prevents adoption. It keeps the branch, PR, source identity, spent repair rounds and configured cycle minimum. The source logbook stays unchanged. Source verdicts do not count: destination reviews and QA start fresh, with the larger source or current destination cycle requirement. An exact retry keeps the recorded adoption and current task state (T44).

## 2026-10-25

- **A lead's wait no longer returns at once in a loop.** When a review or QA helper stopped with a report that the hook cannot read and another helper still ran, the lead's wait command returned at once each time, and the lead could not end that run: only the sage does. Now the wait leaves out such a run: it names the run once, with what to do, and waits for the helpers that still run, up to its 9 minutes. When no helper runs, it returns with the list of these runs. The lead names each one in its report as a gap, and ends blocked only when no helper of its own runs. The text of the hook that blocks a lead's stop now says when the wait returns.
- **The Codex guide names the 4 approval prompts of each task.** With autopilot on in Codex, each task still asks you before 4 commands: create the task worktree, commit, push the task branch and open the pull request. Codex asks, because its `workspace-write` sandbox keeps `.git` read-only and the network off; the verified merge asks nothing. The [Codex guide](docs/guide/codex.md#the-approval-prompts-of-each-task) gives Codex's own choices, quoted from its source. It tells you to choose "Yes, proceed" at each of the 4 prompts, every time, and never "don't ask again" at any Codex prompt: each command runs git, and git can run the project's own code outside the sandbox. sage writes no Codex rule and changes nothing in your Codex config.
- **The Codex chief ends each run on the first try.** Codex gives no token count for an agent, so the state tool ends such a run only with `usage` unavailable, `usage-source`, `usage-evidence` and `report`, and no `tokens`. The chief learned these fields only from a refusal, and until then the open runs held the merge. Now the `run_done` tool's description and the chief's dispatch step name each field and give an example call. The Codex chief cannot write the pages folder from its sandbox, so the `pages` tool now saves a run's report itself: give it the task, the run and the report as `text`, and it saves `<R>-report.md` in the task's pages folder, records it, and prints the path for `run_done`. It refuses an empty report and a run of another task, and it never replaces a saved report. The CLI form is `sage pages <T> record --run <R> --text <report>`. The rule of `run done` did not change.
- **Two speed tests of the hook no longer fail on a slow machine.** The 1 MB padding test compares the time of 1000 KB with the time of 100 KB on the same machine, and its only fixed cap is the hook's own 10 s budget: a fixed 2 s cap failed a correct hook on a slow CI runner. The path work tests count filesystem calls as before, but no fixed 120 s timeout kills their child: the test's own timeout stops a hang, and each input shape is now a test of its own.
- **Every task has a priority.** `task add` (and the Codex `task_add` tool) now refuses a task with no priority or a bad one, writes nothing, and says the scale in one line: P0 the owner's current focus and what blocks it; P1 next (function or safety bugs, work in flight, pre-pilot items); P2 later (polish, hardening lows, follow-ups); P3 parked but kept. `task <T> set priority=none` no longer clears the priority of an open task; an ended task's still clears. A follow-up task of `finding move` gets P2. Older open tasks with no priority still work: `show status` names them on a `priority` line, and their board cards show a "no priority" tag, so that the chief sets one.
- **A task moved off a shared pull request's branch gets a way back that works.** When two tasks share one pull request and the chief moves one of them to another branch, the merge check still refuses that pull request. Its refusal now gives the command that puts the task back on the head branch (`task <T> set branch=<the head branch>`), and first the same command for the task whose name the branch carries, when no task names the branch by its `branch=`. Before, it said to rename the branch to a task name, which leaves the other task behind. A head branch that is the branch of no task still gets the rename advice. The sage hook now also refuses a lead's `run add` on a branch that another task uses after the chief moved the lead's task off it, and the refusal names that move.
- **The chief's rules in Codex have room to grow.** Codex counts a hook's text at 4 bytes a token and cuts it above the hook's limit. The two native parts of the chief text now use Codex's real limit of 10000 bytes each, where sage used 7500, so a small change to the chief's rules no longer refuses them. `npm run check` now fails, with the size and what to do, when the chief text does not fit the sage hook or the native parts.
- **One change log file for each pull request.** A pull request now writes its change log entry in its own file, `changes/<task>.md` (for example `changes/T492.md`), with the date and the list item. `npm run build` puts the entries into this changelog, newest date first, and `npm run check` fails when this changelog is not what the build makes. So the entries of two pull requests no longer conflict as text: a conflict in `CHANGELOG.md` is now only in a built file, and `npm run build` ends it. The build stops, and writes nothing, when `changes/` holds a file that is not a `.md` file or when `CHANGELOG.md` holds a line that you wrote by hand, in any form; its message names the file or the line and says what to do, so no entry drops without a message. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#the-readme-and-the-docs).
- **Every review and QA finding names its run and class.** `finding add` (and the Codex `finding_add` tool) now refuses a finding whose source is a review or QA role (code-reviewer, security-reviewer, ux-reviewer, qa or evidence-review) without `--run` and `--class`, and the refusal names the classes. A known key that opens again keeps its run and class. A finding from another source, such as the sage's own note, may still leave them out. So `sage stats` can count review findings by class and by cycle from now on; older rows do not change. The sage's finding for a failed CI check names the task's lead run and the class other.
- **A lead waits for its helpers, keeps its slot, and runs up to 9 helpers.** The sage hook now blocks a lead's stop while one of its helpers runs, and names the lead's new wait command (`node <plugin>/hooks/wait.mjs <T>`). That command needs only Bash: it returns when a helper stops, with the RESULT that the hook kept from its report; for an implementer, its RESULT word and the head that it left on the branch, so that the lead ends its run and starts the reviews there. A lead's slot holds while its lead run runs, however long it waits, in the session that started it. After a restart or a crash, a new session starts a fresh lead for the task: the old session's lead slot frees after an hour with no event of that lead or its helpers, or at once when the sage ends the old lead run and records a new one. The sage's `run done` of a helper run frees that helper's slot at once, also after a restart and a fresh lead's start, and a lead whose lead run the sage ended may stop while its helpers run. A lead runs up to 9 helpers at once (before: 3), within the project's agent cap, and a refusal at a cap names the lead's wait command. The default caps are now 10 agents for each project (`max_agents`, before: 4), so one lead and its 9 helpers fit, and 20 in all (`cap_total`, before: 12); a value in `config.json` still wins. The hook now refuses a lead's checks verdict, the sage's message to a lead that ended (start a fresh lead), and the sage's review or QA verdict on a task with a running lead run unless a finished run of that task, of the role that gives the kind, backs it with its helper's kept report.
- **Harder Codex rules.** The Codex hook now also blocks these ways around a sage rule:
  - a role agent's message to another thread: `send_input` (multi-agent v1), and `send_message` and `followup_task` (multi-agent v2, in the default `collaboration` namespace), because a message to the chief's thread would count as typed by you, and a reviewer's message could make the implementer change the branch. The chief, and agents without a `sage_` name, send as usual;
  - an agent's `logbook repair` and `standing add` from the shell, which write the logbook;
  - a name of the sage folder or of a `.codex` folder behind quotes (`.co""dex`), `~`, `$HOME` or `$CODEX_HOME`, or from the folder that the command runs in.
  - Not blocked, and written in the guide's limits list: a role agent's start of Codex through text or a script piped into a shell or an interpreter, through a copy of codex (made in the same command or an earlier one), through a link to codex made in the same command, or through text that hides the word codex; and an agent's run of the state tool's write commands from `node -e`, `node -` (standard input), after a `node` option, as a module to load, or from a copied script. Codex's sandbox is the stop: in workspace-write, network access is off for the session, and the Codex home and the logbook are read-only.
  - A `node` script whose name only has the state tool's name in it (`node src/message.mjs`), or that gets the tool's path as data (`node scripts/lint.mjs <tool>`), runs again for every agent. So do normal commands that name codex, such as `~/bin/tool codex`, `pushd packages/sage-codex && ../../node_modules/.bin/esbuild …` and `cat codex.json | python3 -mjson.tool`.
  - The brief tool's message now names each field form that the check takes: a colon, two spaces or a tab after the name, or the name alone on its line.
  - The brief check now starts a field only at a line that is the field's name with a colon (`FORBIDDEN:`), two spaces or a tab after it, or nothing, outside a list or a code block. So a line such as "FORBIDDEN words are flagged" in another field no longer gives a role agent the wrong `FORBIDDEN` text.
  - The chief's setup text in Codex now says that the state CLI only reads (`board`, `config`), and that `program` has no tool yet, so programs do not run in Codex. The limits that stay are in [sage in Codex](docs/guide/codex.md#the-rules-in-codex).
- **Three README lines now match the facts.** The status line says that CI runs the tests on Ubuntu (Linux), where it said that Linux was not tested. The Quick start gives Node.js 20 as the minimum and says that CI runs Node 24. The Codex install line now lists a GitHub remote for the project beside `gh`, and the board image's alt text says "program items". The on phrase step says which words to send, and the update warning says what a program and a wait are before it uses them.
- **Two tasks can share one pull request under autopilot.** The chief can now give a second task the branch of another task (`task <T> set branch=<the other task's branch>`), with the same `pr=`. Autopilot merges that pull request when each task passes on its own verdicts. Before, the merge check refused it, because its head branch was not named for each task, so you merged it yourself. The merge check still refuses when a task of that branch is not on the pull request, or when one task of the pull request names another branch. A lead still names only a branch of its own task, and only the chief puts a task on a shared branch or takes it off one, also a branch named for the lead's task when another task names it or ran work on it. A task that ran work on a branch stays an owner of it after it moves to another branch, so it must be on that pull request too. The PR script's merge runs the same head branch check as the hook. When a task that owns the head branch is not on the pull request, the refusal says how it owns the branch (by its name, by a run on it, or by its `branch=`), and it says to move the task to another branch only when that works: when it owns the branch by its `branch=` alone.
- **Leads start again in the desktop app.** The sage hook refused every lead start in the Claude desktop app, because its Agent tool has no `name` and no `run_in_background` field. Now the hook reads a lead's name `lead-T<n>` from the first word of the description when no name is sent, and refuses only `run_in_background` false. A lead names each helper by its run id `R<n>` in the same way. The chief starts a lead with a description such as `lead-T12 fix the form`, and stops or messages a lead with no name by its agent id: the hook refuses a stop by `lead-T<n>` for such a lead.
- **Waits in the chat's task lookup and on the programs list.** When you ask about a task that waits, the chat now gives the task page's Now and Next lines: for example "Waits for T10 (abandoned): it cannot start", and "Next: Nothing until the wait changes". Before, it said "In the backlog" and "Next: The build". On the programs list and in the chat's programs lines, a program whose breakdown waits for you, or that the chief revises, now names each task that cannot start.
- **A replay of past reviews.** `node scripts/review-replay.mjs <logbook folder> [--out <file>]` reads a logbook and reports, for the 10 merged PRs with the most review data, which review roles ran, their tokens by repair round, their findings by severity, class and round, which findings came after round 0 or moved to a later task, and which roles found nothing; then the findings per million tokens for each role and class, and the gaps in the data. A finding that moved to a follow-up task counts once, on the task where a review found it. It only reads the logbook, and it refuses to write its report there, also through a link or another letter case of the path. It changes no route: it measures, so that you can decide which reviews to keep for a project.
- **Clearer sage lines in Codex.** A refusal of a sage rule no longer ends with two periods before Codex's "Command:" text. A refusal for Codex's approval check calls it the approval check. The chief's line for the state tool says that its shell command is for reads only, and that the chief writes the logbook only with the sage MCP tools. A fault line says to update the sage plugin and to keep Codex in the tested range (0.160 to 0.164). The [Codex guide](docs/guide/codex.md) now lists `gh` under What you need, and it says how to stop merges at once (press Esc, then send the off phrase for autopilot), what to do when the hook cannot read Codex's record of a thread, how to update a local clone, and that the Codex logbook stays after a removal. Its `write_stdin` limit now says that autopilot off does not stop such a merge.
- **Autopilot and the version line in a long Codex session.** In a Codex session whose transcript is over about 512 MiB, autopilot now stays on, so the hook still allows a verified merge. Before, the hook could not read so large a file, read autopilot as off, and refused the merge. A resumed long session also shows its Codex version again, with no false warning. The hook now reads the transcript in pieces, and the version from the first line only.
- **A shorter README.** The README has a "Why sage?" section again, after the hero image. The Status, Requirements and What's new sections are gone. The status line at the top gives the maturity and the systems, each requirement is in the text where you need it (the Quick start and the board), and this changelog alone lists the changes. In the `readme-guide` skill, a link to the changelog now counts as the What's new section.
- **sage on Codex.** sage now runs in your normal Codex CLI, as one plugin. The Codex desktop app should work the same way, but it is not checked yet.
  - Install: add the sage marketplace with `codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/erickb336/sage.git`, install with `codex plugin add sage@sage`, and choose "Trust all and continue" at Codex's "Hooks need review" screen. These are Codex CLI commands, so a desktop app user needs the Codex CLI too. Each session then gives the chief one status: the sage version, the Codex version, how many of the 10 sage hooks have your trust, and the on phrase (or that sage mode is on, in a resumed session). You see a warning only when a sage hook has no trust yet or your Codex is outside the tested range (0.160 to 0.164).
  - sage mode: `sage mode` alone gives the session the chief's role, and the role comes back after each compaction. `sage mode off`, `autopilot on`, `autopilot off` and `sage help` work as in Claude Code, from the same rules in the shared core. A damaged mode file is off, and a forked thread starts off.
  - The logbook tools: a local MCP server, `sage`, gives the state tool's commands as tools (`init`, `status`, `task_add`, `verdict`, `merge_check` and the others), with the same checks. The plugin approves its own tools, so they ask you nothing.
  - Role agents: the chief starts each role agent as a Codex child agent, with the role text at the top of its spawn message and a task name `sage_<role>_t<n>_r<k>` (the role, the task and the run id, so that a second run of a role gets a new name). The chief does the lead's work for now. Role agents start no agents and record nothing in the logbook: they report, and the chief records. A role agent's report without every field (`STATUS` to `BRANCH`) gets one more turn.
  - The brief check: before each spawn, the chief runs the new `brief` tool, which names each missing field (`GOAL` to `STANDING`) and keeps the brief in the logbook. Each role agent starts with the project's standing orders, the `FORBIDDEN` field and its checked brief, or with a line that no checked brief is on record. After a spawn with no checked brief, the chief gets a warning. The check does not block a spawn.
  - The rules: in sage mode the chief changes no files with `apply_patch`, and a reviewer and QA, and every agent under them, change no files with `apply_patch` or a plain shell write. A push takes the push form of Claude Code. No one edits a project's `.codex` folder (a project under `~/.codex/worktrees` edits as usual), names the Codex sage folder or sessions folder in a shell command, or resumes or forks a Codex session from the shell. No role agent runs the installed Codex from the shell, starts an agent, or calls a logbook tool that writes. A merge runs only in the form `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit <sha>`, from the main thread.
  - Autopilot merges verified work: the hook allows only the exact merge command when the merge check passes, with no prompt. Autopilot counts only when the mode file and your own typed messages both turn it on. Every other approval gets Codex's own prompt.
  - Codex's own review thread (`/review`, the app's review button) and its approval check share the session with the chief, but the hook reads Codex's record of each thread: they count as read-only role agents, so they record nothing in the logbook, start no agents and start no Codex. An agent whose record the hook cannot read is read-only too. A role agent's `rg` (Codex's own copy) and `codex --version` run, and a command such as `$EDITOR codex/a.txt` runs, except for a role agent while the mode is on.
  - A limit: Codex 0.164.0 runs no hook for text that an agent types into a shell that still runs (`write_stdin`), so that text passes every sage rule, also a push or a merge. In workspace-write, the sandbox keeps this text off the network and keeps the logbook closed: keep network access off, and refuse an interactive shell outside the sandbox. Autopilot off does not stop such a merge. See the limits in [sage in Codex](docs/guide/codex.md#the-rules-in-codex).
  - Checked with the Codex CLI 0.160.0 and 0.164.0 and a test model on this machine, not yet in the desktop app. See [sage in Codex](docs/guide/codex.md).

Before, sage mode came back on at the next event, and the session had no file tools.
